name: DocVQA
description: A dataset for Visual Question Answering on document images consisting of 50,000 questions defined on 12,767 document images of varied types and content.
creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
citeAs: Mathew, Minesh, Dimosthenis Karatzas, and C.V. Jawahar. "DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images." arXiv:2007.00398v3, 2021.
rai:dataCollection: Document images were sourced from documents in the UCSF Industry Documents Library. The authors downloaded documents from different collections and hand picked pages for use in the dataset, prioritizing pages with tables, forms, lists and figures and trying to minimize binarized images because poor image quality could be a bottleneck for VQA. Questions and answers were collected with the help of remote workers using a web-based annotation tool in three stages: in stage 1 workers defined at most 10 question-answer pairs per image and could add more than one ground truth answer per question; in stage 2 another worker verified by answering the questions without seeing stage 1 answers and assigned one or more question types, with an option to flag inapt questions; in stage 3, questions with answer mismatches between stages 1 and 2 were reviewed by the authors, who could edit and accept or ignore them.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images in the dataset are sourced from documents in the UCSF Industry Documents Library. The final set of images are drawn from pages of 6,071 industry documents spanning 1900 to 2018 across five industries: tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel and chemical.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors downloaded documents from different collections and hand picked pages from these documents for use in the dataset. They tried to minimize binarized images and prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists and figures over pages with only running text. The data was split randomly in an 80-10-10 ratio into train, validation and test splits.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions flagged in stage 2 as inapt owing to language issues or ambiguity were not included in the dataset. If none of the answers entered in stage 1 matched exactly with any answers from stage 2, the question was sent for review in stage 3, where the authors could edit the question and answers before accepting or ignoring it.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions and answers were collected with remote workers using a web-based annotation tool. In stage 1, workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs on it, asking questions answerable using text present in the image and entering the answer verbatim from the document; workers were encouraged to add more than one ground truth answer per question when warranted. In stage 2, a different worker was shown the image and the questions from stage 1, but not the stage 1 answers, and was required to enter answers and assign one or more question types to each question. If stage 1 and stage 2 answers did not match exactly, the question went to a third stage where the authors reviewed, edited if necessary, and either accepted or ignored the question-answer pair.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The second annotation stage verified the data collected in the first stage. Questions could be flagged for language issues or ambiguity and such questions were excluded. If none of the answers from stage 1 matched exactly with any answers from stage 2, the question was sent for a third-stage review by the authors, who could edit questions and answers before accepting or ignoring them.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 10 question-answer pairs could be defined per document image in stage 1; each question was answered by at least two annotators across stages 1 and 2, with additional author review in mismatch cases.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Remote workers; for human performance on the test split, answers were collected with help of a few volunteers from the authors' institution.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: A commercial OCR application; a commercial OCR solution
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, code and leaderboard are available at docvqa.org.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and task aim to inspire a 'purpose-driven' approach in document image analysis and recognition research and could drive methods that use low-level cues and high-level goals in solving problems of practical importance.
rai:dataBiases: The authors prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists and figures over pages with only running text. They also tried to minimize binarized images and used many documents from food and nutrition related collections because they had a good number of non-binarized images. Most documents are from the 1960-2000 period.
rai:dataLimitations: Majority of documents in the source library are binarized and binarization has taken a toll on image quality. The authors tried to minimize such images because poor image quality could be a bottleneck for VQA. The paper also notes that models need to improve specifically on questions where understanding structure of the document is crucial, and that better understanding of figures, text on photographs, and handwriting is needed.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for Visual Question Answering on document images and for evaluating baseline methods. It is split into train, validation and test sets in an 80-10-10 ratio: train has 39,463 questions and 10,194 images, validation has 5,349 questions and 1,286 images, and test has 5,188 questions and 1,287 images.
